Default transaction classification rules

Source: R/classify.R
merger_rules.Rd

Thresholds used by classify_transactions(). Override any element to run stricter or broader definitions.

Usage

merger_rules(
  min_top_share = 0.75,
  leader = c("either", "sn", "p7"),
  min_donors_n = 2L,
  new_entity_years = 1L,
  sn_text = TRUE,
  promote = FALSE,
  min_corroborate = 2L,
  corroborate = c("SO_MERGER_TEXT_DONOR", "SO_MERGER_TEXT_RECIP", "GOV_DOC_CHANGE_RECIP"),
  final_as_termination = TRUE
)

Arguments

min_top_share

Minimum share of transferred FMV going to the dominant nonprofit recipient for a dissolution to count as a transfer to one successor (rather than a dispersed closure). When FMV is missing, a single nonprofit recipient counts as one successor. The default of 0.75 comes from hand validation: every sampled dissolution with a top share between 0.5 and 0.75 was read as a dispersed closure.

leader

Leadership-continuity evidence: "either" (Schedule N lines 2a-2c or Part VII overlap, the default), "sn" (Schedule N flags only), or "p7" (Part VII overlap only).

min_donors_n

Number of dissolving donors to one recipient in the same window that makes a merger mergerN.

new_entity_years

A recipient formed within this many years before the merger year counts as a new entity (consolidation).

sn_text

If TRUE (default), merger language in Schedule N's own text (SN_MERGER_TEXT, see sn_merger_pattern()) counts as merger evidence on its own, like leadership continuity.

promote

If TRUE, a dissolution to one nonprofit successor with no leadership evidence is promoted from asset_transfer to a merger label when at least min_corroborate corroborating signals agree. Off by default: in hand validation only 1 of 13 promoted filings read as a merger. The signals are still computed, so promotion can be turned on for a broad definition.

min_corroborate

Number of corroborating signals required for promotion. One signal alone was too loose on 2019-21 data; two promoted about 5% of asset transfers, and those looked like mergers on measures the rule does not use.

corroborate

Names of logical columns that count as corroborating signals: Schedule O merger language on the donor's and the recipient's return, and a Part VI line 4 governing-document change at the recipient in year t or t+1.

final_as_termination

If TRUE (default), a filing with only Part II (disposition of more than 25% of assets) but the final-return box checked is treated as a termination, like a Part I filing. In hand validation none of these were ongoing dispositions; most were mergers or transfers at dissolution reported on the wrong part.

Value

A list of class merger_rules.

Examples

merger_rules()
#> $min_top_share
#> [1] 0.75
#> 
#> $leader
#> [1] "either"
#> 
#> $final_as_termination
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $sn_text
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $min_donors_n
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $new_entity_years
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $promote
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $min_corroborate
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $corroborate
#> [1] "SO_MERGER_TEXT_DONOR" "SO_MERGER_TEXT_RECIP" "GOV_DOC_CHANGE_RECIP"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "merger_rules"
merger_rules(leader = "sn", sn_text = FALSE)
#> $min_top_share
#> [1] 0.75
#> 
#> $leader
#> [1] "sn"
#> 
#> $final_as_termination
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $sn_text
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $min_donors_n
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $new_entity_years
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $promote
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $min_corroborate
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $corroborate
#> [1] "SO_MERGER_TEXT_DONOR" "SO_MERGER_TEXT_RECIP" "GOV_DOC_CHANGE_RECIP"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "merger_rules"
merger_rules(promote = TRUE)   # broad definition
#> $min_top_share
#> [1] 0.75
#> 
#> $leader
#> [1] "either"
#> 
#> $final_as_termination
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $sn_text
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $min_donors_n
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $new_entity_years
#> [1] 1

#> [1] TRUE
